claims.claim: ADH1C, SCARA5, and CFD were observed mostly in adventitial region marked by PDGFRA.
claims.source: In the pulmonary artery compartment, RGS5 and IGFBP5 positivity overlapped predominantly with ACTA2 (alpha smooth muscle actin) stain, while ADH1C, SCARA5, and CFD were observed mostly in adventitial region marked by PDGFRA (Platelet-Derived Growth Factor Receptor Alpha) (Figure 1D, E).
claims.evidence: This is supported by multicolor immunofluorescent staining and in situ hybridization shown in Figure 1D and E.

claims.claim: PASMC showed enrichment in vascular development and cell migration processes.
claims.source: The analysis confirmed polarized and distinct cell-type functional associations, revealing vascular development and cell migration processes for PASMC, and endoplasmatic reticulum protein targeting for PAAF.
claims.evidence: This is based on GSEA on GO terms for biological processes using integrated transcriptomic and proteomic data (Figure 1F).

claims.claim: PAAF showed enrichment in endoplasmatic reticulum protein targeting processes.
claims.source: The analysis confirmed polarized and distinct cell-type functional associations, revealing vascular development and cell migration processes for PASMC, and endoplasmatic reticulum protein targeting for PAAF.
claims.evidence: This is based on GSEA on GO terms for biological processes using integrated transcriptomic and proteomic data (Figure 1F).

claims.claim: PASMC was associated with processes linked to sterol transport, O-glycosylation, and nerve growth factor signaling.
claims.source: Additionally, PASMC was associated with processes linked to sterol transport, O-glycosylation, and nerve growth factor signaling (Figure 1F).
claims.evidence: This is based on GSEA analysis shown in Figure 1F.

claims.claim: PAAF showed enrichment in mitochondrial metabolic processes and heavy metal ion detoxification.
claims.source: PAAF on the other hand showed enrichment in mitochondrial metabolic processes and heavy metal ion detoxification (Figure 1F).
claims.evidence: This is based on GSEA analysis shown in Figure 1F.

claims.claim: PASMC showed enrichment for ECM organization among top10 biological processes.
claims.source: Contrasting the canonical functional roles, it was PASMC, rather than PAAF, that showed enrichment for ECM organization (Figure 1G), while PAAF showed enrichment for heavy metal ion response, lipid homeostasis, and cell differentiation (Figure 1G).
claims.evidence: This is based on overrepresentation analysis of GO biological processes shown in Figure 1G.

claims.claim: PAAF showed enrichment for heavy metal ion response, lipid homeostasis, and cell differentiation.
claims.source: Contrasting the canonical functional roles, it was PASMC, rather than PAAF, that showed enrichment for ECM organization (Figure 1G), while PAAF showed enrichment for heavy metal ion response, lipid homeostasis, and cell differentiation (Figure 1G).
claims.evidence: This is based on overrepresentation analysis of GO biological processes shown in Figure 1G.

claims.claim: PASMC could equally utilize glucose/pyruvate and long chain fatty acids as a fuel source for oxidative metabolism.
claims.source: Real-time monitoring of oxygen consumption under basal condition and upon specific metabolic inhibitors revealed that PASMC could equally utilize glucose/pyruvate and long chain fatty acids as a fuel source for oxidative metabolism (Figure 1H1).
claims.evidence: This is supported by Seahorse metabolic analyzer measurements shown in Figure 1H.

claims.claim: PAAF had stronger drop in basal respiration rate upon blocking fatty acid utilization in Krebs cycle compared to PASMC.
claims.source: In contrast, upon blocking fatty acid utilization in Krebs cycle, PAAF had stronger drop in basal respiration rate while PASMC was less sensitive to this maneuver (Figure 1I).
claims.evidence: This is supported by Seahorse metabolic analyzer measurements with etomoxir shown in Figure 1I.

claims.claim: PAAF had lower OCR and ECAR compared to PASMC.
claims.source: PAAF had lower OCR and ECAR (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
claims.evidence: This is supported by Seahorse metabolic measurements shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claims.claim: PAAF has relative preference for oxidative phosphorylation compared to PASMC.
claims.source: Ratio of oxygen consumption to extracellular acidification (OCR/ECAR) revealed that PAAF has relative preference for oxidative phosphorylation compared to PASMC (Figure 1—figure supplement 2), in line with observed enrichment for mitochondrial respiration processes (Figure 1F).
claims.evidence: This is supported by OCR/ECAR ratio measurements shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claims.claim: PAAF had lower glycolytic capacity compared to PASMC.
claims.source: This was further supported by lower glycolytic capacity (Figure 1—figure supplement 2) and lower mitochondrial proton leak (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
claims.evidence: This is supported by Seahorse metabolic measurements shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claims.claim: PAAF had lower mitochondrial proton leak compared to PASMC.
claims.source: This was further supported by lower glycolytic capacity (Figure 1—figure supplement 2) and lower mitochondrial proton leak (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
claims.evidence: This is supported by Seahorse metabolic measurements shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claims.claim: Sample separation based on disease state was less obvious than separation based on cell type in PCA analysis.
claims.source: PCA analysis of transcriptomic and proteomic profiles revealed a clear sample separation based on cell type (Figure 2A). However, sample separation based on disease state was less obvious (Figure 2A).
claims.evidence: This is observed in the PCA plots shown in Figure 2A.

claims.claim: OPLS-DA modeling found significant differences in the global transcriptomics and proteomics profiles based only on the cell type, but not disease state.
claims.source: OPLS-DA modeling found significant differences in the global transcriptomics and proteomics profiles based only on the cell type, but not disease state (Figure 2B), validating PCA analysis observations.
claims.evidence: This is based on supervised multivariate OPLS-DA analysis shown in Figure 2B.

claims.claim: Only in the case of transcriptomic dataset there was significant separation between all four groups when considering both cell type and disease state simultaneously in OPLS-DA model.
claims.source: In this OPLA-DA model, only in the case of transcriptomic dataset there was significant separation between all four groups (Figure 2C).
claims.evidence: This is based on bifactorial OPLS-DA analysis shown in Figure 2C.

claims.claim: Remodeling process results in substantial transcriptional changes (cell state), but each cell type retains their original cell lineage designation.
claims.source: These results imply that remodeling process results in substantial transcriptional changes (cell state), but that each cell type retains their original cell lineage designation, in line with results from fate mapping and fresh cell single-cell transcriptomics (Biasin et al., 2020; Crnkovic et al., 2022; Crnkovic et al., 2018).
claims.evidence: This is inferred from OPLS-DA results and supported by citations to fate mapping and single-cell studies.

claims.claim: IPAH-PASMC were characterized by upregulation of nucleotide-sugar and lipid biosynthesis, Golgi vesicle transport and endoplasmic reticulum stress processes.
claims.source: IPAH-PASMC were characterized by upregulation of nucleotide-sugar and lipid biosynthesis, Golgi vesicle transport and endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress processes, while simultaneously displaying downregulation of cytoskeletal components, ribonucleoprotein complex export and p53 signaling (Figure 3A).
claims.evidence: This is based on GO analysis of combined transcriptomic and proteomic data shown in Figure 3A.

claims.claim: IPAH-PASMC displayed downregulation of cytoskeletal components, ribonucleoprotein complex export and p53 signaling.
claims.source: IPAH-PASMC were characterized by upregulation of nucleotide-sugar and lipid biosynthesis, Golgi vesicle transport and endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress processes, while simultaneously displaying downregulation of cytoskeletal components, ribonucleoprotein complex export and p53 signaling (Figure 3A).
claims.evidence: This is based on GO analysis of combined transcriptomic and proteomic data shown in Figure 3A.

claims.claim: IPAH-PAAF upregulated genes and proteins involved in cell proliferation and DNA repair.
claims.source: IPAH-PAAF upregulated genes and proteins involved in cell proliferation, DNA repair and downregulated expression of NF-κB pathway components, NK-cell activation, and transcriptional stress response (Figure 3A).
claims.evidence: This is based on GO analysis of combined transcriptomic and proteomic data shown in Figure 3A.

claims.claim: IPAH-PAAF downregulated expression of NF-κB pathway components, NK-cell activation, and transcriptional stress response.
claims.source: IPAH-PAAF upregulated genes and proteins involved in cell proliferation, DNA repair and downregulated expression of NF-κB pathway components, NK-cell activation, and transcriptional stress response (Figure 3A).
claims.evidence: This is based on GO analysis of combined transcriptomic and proteomic data shown in Figure 3A.

claims.claim: IPAH PA had increased GAG content compared to donor PA.
claims.source: Quantitative analysis revealed increased GAG content in IPAH (n = 8) compared to donor (n = 7) PA (Figure 3B).
claims.evidence: This is supported by 1,9-dimethylmethylene blue assay measurements shown in Figure 3B.

claims.claim: IPAH PA showed enhanced medial staining and prominent signal in neointimal compartment for glycosaminoglycans.
claims.source: This showed enhanced medial staining in IPAH (n = 10) compared to donor (n = 10) and prominent signal in neointimal PA compartment (Figure 3C) that was confirmed by quantitative image analysis (Figure 3D).
claims.evidence: This is supported by Alcian blue staining and quantitative image analysis shown in Figure 3C and 3D.

claims.claim: IPAH-PAAF displayed higher proliferative capacity compared to donor-PAAF upon both stimulated and unstimulated conditions.
claims.source: In line with observed enrichment for DNA replication and cell cycle phase regulation (Figure 3A), IPAH-PAAF displayed higher proliferative capacity compared to donor–PAAF, upon both stimulated and unstimulated conditions (Figure 3E).
claims.evidence: This is supported by [3H]thymidine incorporation assay shown in Figure 3E.

claims.claim: IPAH-PASMC showed lower proliferative rate compared to donor-PASMC.
claims.source: IPAH-PASMC in contrary showed lower proliferative rate compared to donor–PASMC (Figure 3E), corresponding to our previous observation of G1 cell cycle accumulation of IPAH-PASMC (Crnkovic et al., 2022).
claims.evidence: This is supported by [3H]thymidine incorporation assay shown in Figure 3E and cited previous study.

claims.claim: The observed phenotypic effect of differential proliferation is strongest in very early passage and is progressively lost with passaging.
claims.source: The observed phenotypic effect is strongest in very early passage and is progressively lost with passaging (Figure 3F).
claims.evidence: This is supported by cell counting data across passages shown in Figure 3F.

claims.claim: PCNA+ fibroblasts were frequently observed in the adventitial layer of PA from IPAH patients.
claims.source: We observed frequent PCNA+ fibroblasts, identified by PDGFRA staining, in the adventitial layer of PA from IPAH patients (Figure 3G), while decreased percentage of proliferating PASMC in IPAH PA, detected by PCNA and Ki-67 staining, was reported previously (Crnkovic et al., 2022).
claims.evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescent staining shown in Figure 3G.

claims.claim: Early-passage IPAH-PASMC retain positive enrichment for biosynthetic and ECM processes.
claims.source: Early-passage IPAH-PASMC (p1) retain positive enrichment for biosynthetic and ECM processes and share positive enrichment for macrophage regulation processes with fresh cells, while simultaneously displaying gradual negative enrichment of contraction associated processes (Figure 3H).
claims.evidence: This is based on GSEA analysis comparing fresh, early-passage, and late-passage cells shown in Figure 3H.

claims.claim: Both early and late-passage IPAH-PAAF display prominent positive enrichment for cell cycle and proliferation processes.
claims.source: Surprisingly, both early (p1)- and late-passage (p6) IPAH-PAAF display prominent positive enrichment for cell cycle and proliferation processes, with fresh cells showing weak enrichment for DNA recombination process (Figure 3H).
claims.evidence: This is based on GSEA analysis comparing fresh, early-passage, and late-passage cells shown in Figure 3H.

claims.claim: There are prominent inverse enrichments for inflammatory/NF-κB signaling between fresh and cultured IPAH-PAAF.
claims.source: Even more striking are prominent inverse enrichments for inflammatory/NF-κB signaling between fresh and cultured IPAH-PAAF (Figure 3H).
claims.evidence: This is based on GSEA analysis comparing fresh and cultured cells shown in Figure 3H.

claims.claim: Number of co-directionally regulated genes and proteins between IPAH-PASMC and IPAH-PAAF were limited to 47.
claims.source: Number of co-directionally regulated genes and proteins were limited to 47 (Figure 4A).
claims.evidence: This is based on analysis of differentially expressed genes and proteins shown in Figure 4A.

claims.claim: Regulatory nodes of commonly regulated genes and proteins converged on immuno-inflammatory and survival-apoptosis regulators and effectors.
claims.source: Interestingly, their regulatory nodes converged on the immuno-inflammatory and survival-apoptosis regulators and effectors (Figure 4C).
claims.evidence: This is based on STRING-based interaction network analysis shown in Figure 4C.

claims.claim: Regulation of apoptosis is a shared pathway by both PASMC and PAAF in IPAH.
claims.source: Additional pathway enrichment analysis based on the BioPlanet database, uncovered regulation of apoptosis as a shared pathway by both cell types in IPAH (Figure 4D).
claims.evidence: This is based on pathway enrichment analysis shown in Figure 4D.

claims.claim: Cellular mitochondrial content was lower both in IPAH-PASMC and IPAH-PAAF upon starvation.
claims.source: Cellular mitochondrial content was lower both in IPAH-PASMC and IPAH-PAAF upon removal of serum and growth factors (starvation) (Figure 4E).
claims.evidence: This is supported by TMRM staining measurements shown in Figure 4E.

claims.claim: The remaining mitochondria in IPAH cells were hyperpolarized.
claims.source: However, the remaining mitochondria in IPAH cells were hyperpolarized (Figure 4F).
claims.evidence: This is supported by TMRM-based mitochondrial membrane potential measurements shown in Figure 4F.

claims.claim: Only IPAH-PASMC significantly upregulate ROS production upon PDGF-BB stimulation.
claims.source: We measured cellular ROS production using CellRox Deep Red dye at basal levels and upon PDGF-BB stimulation revealing that only IPAH-PASMC significantly upregulate ROS production (Figure 4G).
claims.evidence: This is supported by CellRox measurements shown in Figure 4G.

claims.claim: PASMC possessed more pronounced changes than PAAF as shown by the number of differentially regulated genes and proteins in IPAH.
claims.source: PASMC possessed more pronounced changes than PAAF as shown by the number of differentially regulated genes and proteins in IPAH (Figure 5B).
claims.evidence: This is based on analysis of differentially regulated elements shown in Figure 5B.

claims.claim: The majority of downregulated molecules in IPAH-PASMC came from a set of genes and proteins preferentially expressed by PASMC in healthy state.
claims.source: A STRING-based interaction network, overlaid with information about the initial cell-type association under normal condition (preferential enrichment in donor–PASMC or PAAF) (Figure 5B), revealed that the majority of downregulated molecules in IPAH-PASMC came from a set of genes and proteins preferentially expressed by PASMC in healthy state (donor–PASMC) (Figure 5B).
claims.evidence: This is based on STRING-based interaction network analysis shown in Figure 5B.

claims.claim: Molecules upregulated in IPAH-PASMC contained targets from both PASMC- and PAAF-enriched dataset under healthy cell states.
claims.source: In contrast, molecules upregulated in IPAH-PASMC contained targets from both PASMC- and PAAF-enriched dataset under healthy cell states (donors).
claims.evidence: This is based on analysis of upregulated molecules in IPAH-PASMC and their origin from donor cell types.

claims.claim: IPAH-regulated molecules in PAAF could be traced back to both PASMC- and PAAF-enriched normal cell state.
claims.source: IPAH-regulated molecules in PAAF on the other hand could be traced back to both PASMC- and PAAF-enriched normal cell state (Figure 5B).
claims.evidence: This is based on analysis of regulated molecules in IPAH-PAAF and their origin from donor cell types shown in Figure 5B.

claims.claim: PASMC harbored expression changes in biological processes related to ECM in IPAH.
claims.source: GO analysis of IPAH revealed a clear cell-type distinct fingerprint of molecular changes: PASMC harbored expression changes in biological processes related to ECM, while cell cycle and replication processes were enriched in PAAF (Figure 5C).
claims.evidence: This is based on GO analysis shown in Figure 5C.

claims.claim: Cell cycle and replication processes were enriched in IPAH-PAAF.
claims.source: GO analysis of IPAH revealed a clear cell-type distinct fingerprint of molecular changes: PASMC harbored expression changes in biological processes related to ECM, while cell cycle and replication processes were enriched in PAAF (Figure 5C).
claims.evidence: This is based on GO analysis shown in Figure 5C.

claims.claim: Both PASMC and PAAF on collagen-coated surface had spread-out shape with several protrusions.
claims.source: Whereas cells on collagen-coated surface had spread-out shape with several protrusions (Figure 6C), laminin coating inhibited cell spreading and cells obtained a more symmetric, round-like appearance (Figure 6C).
claims.evidence: This is based on microscopy observations shown in Figure 6C.

claims.claim: Laminin coating inhibited cell spreading and cells obtained a more symmetric, round-like appearance.
claims.source: Whereas cells on collagen-coated surface had spread-out shape with several protrusions (Figure 6C), laminin coating inhibited cell spreading and cells obtained a more symmetric, round-like appearance (Figure 6C).
claims.evidence: This is based on microscopy observations shown in Figure 6C.

claims.claim: PASMC, both donor and IPAH, attached less efficiently to laminin compared to collagen-coated surfaces.
claims.source: PASMC, both donor and IPAH, attached less efficiently to laminin compared to collagen-coated surfaces (Figure 6D), but only donor–PAAF displayed comparable behavior (Figure 6D).
claims.evidence: This is supported by attachment assay data shown in Figure 6D.

claims.claim: Only donor-PAAF displayed lower attachment to laminin compared to collagen-coated surfaces.
claims.source: PASMC, both donor and IPAH, attached less efficiently to laminin compared to collagen-coated surfaces (Figure 6D), but only donor–PAAF displayed comparable behavior (Figure 6D).
claims.evidence: This is supported by attachment assay data shown in Figure 6D.

claims.claim: IPAH-PASMC had tendentially higher attachment on laminin-coated surface compared to donor-PASMC.
claims.source: Although not significant, IPAH-PASMC had tendentially higher attachment on laminin-coated surface compared to donor–PASMC (Figure 6D).
claims.evidence: This is observed in attachment assay data shown in Figure 6D, though not statistically significant.

claims.claim: Donor-PASMC showed widening gap area before final gap closure on laminin coating at early time points.
claims.source: At early time points, donor–PASMC showed widening gap area before final gap closure on laminin coating (Figure 6E).
claims.evidence: This is based on gap closure assay data shown in Figure 6E.

claims.claim: PAAF revealed a faster gap closure compared to PASMC on both collagen and laminin substrates.
claims.source: On both substrates, PAAF revealed a faster gap closure compared to PASMC (Figure 6E), likely in line with their higher proliferative capacity (Figure 3E).
claims.evidence: This is based on gap closure assay data shown in Figure 6E.

claims.claim: The expression profile of integrin subunits serving as high-affinity collagen or laminin receptors was higher in cultured PASMC compared to PAAF.
claims.source: The expression profile of integrin subunits serving as high-affinity collagen (α2β1) or laminin receptors (α3β1 and α6β1) (Moiseeva, 2001) was higher in cultured PASMC compared to PAAF, with minimal change in the disease state (Figure 6F).
claims.evidence: This is based on gene expression data from cultured cells shown in Figure 6F.

claims.claim: IPAH-PAAF displayed increased expression of alpha2 and alpha6 integrin subunits in fresh cells.
claims.source: A similar profile was detected in fresh cell, whereby IPAH-PAAF displayed increased expression of alpha2 and alpha6 subunits (Figure 6G).
claims.evidence: This is based on single-cell transcriptomics data from fresh cells shown in Figure 6G.

claims.claim: Both VCAN and DCN showed a trend or had significantly higher expression level in IPAH cells.
claims.source: Both VCAN (n = 4) and DCN (n = 6) showed a trend or had significantly higher expression level in IPAH cells (Figure 6H, I).
claims.evidence: This is based on gene expression measurements after complement stimulation shown in Figure 6H and I.

claims.claim: Only donor-PAAF responded to C3a and C5a stimulation and displayed IPAH-state-like expression levels of DCN.
claims.source: However, only donor–PAAF responded to C3a and C5a stimulation and displayed IPAH-state-like expression levels of DCN (Figure 6I).
claims.evidence: This is based on gene expression measurements after complement stimulation shown in Figure 6I.

claims.claim: CellChat analysis revealed a skewed PAAF-to-PASMC signaling in IPAH state toward secreted ligands.
claims.source: This revealed a skewed PAAF-to-PASMC signaling in IPAH state toward secreted ligands (Figure 7A, Figure 7—figure supplements 1 and 2).
claims.evidence: This is based on CellChat analysis of single-cell RNA sequencing data shown in Figure 7A and supplements.

claims.claim: Merged CellChat and NicheNet analysis revealed a set of functionally relevant soluble ligands such as IL1A, POSTN, PDGFA/B, FGF2, BMP2/4, CD40LG perturbed in IPAH state.
claims.source: Merged CellChat and NicheNet analysis results revealed a set of functionally relevant soluble ligands such as IL1A, POSTN, PDGFA/B, FGF2, BMP2/4, CD40LG perturbed in IPAH state (Figure 7B).
claims.evidence: This is based on combined CellChat and NicheNet analysis shown in Figure 7B.

claims.claim: Co-culture of donor-PASMC with IPAH-PAAF lead to partial loss of healthy state PASMC markers (CNN1 and RHOA) without affecting the expression of disease-state markers (VCAN and BGN).
claims.source: Results revealed that co-culture of donor–PASMC with IPAH-PAAF (n = 3) lead to partial loss of healthy state PASMC markers (CNN1 and RHOA) without affecting the expression of disease-state markers (VCAN and BGN) (Figure 7D).

claims.claim: Expression of neither healthy nor disease-state PAAF markers was affected in donor-PAAF co-cultured with IPAH-PASMC.

claims.evidence: This is based on qRT-PCR analysis of co-cultured cells shown in Figure 7D.

claims.claim: Genes upregulated in PASMC by IPAH-PAAF co-culture mediate inflammatory processes and signaling, apoptosis, and proliferation.
claims.source: The resulting GSEA on significantly regulated genes (Source data 4) showed that genes upregulated in PASMC by IPAH-PAAF co-culture mediate inflammatory processes and signaling, apoptosis, and proliferation (Figure 7E).
claims.evidence: This is based on GSEA of bulk RNA-Seq data from co-cultured cells shown in Figure 7E.

claims.claim: Stimulation of PASMC with PTX3 preserved the expression of contractile markers in donor cells, but not in IPAH.
claims.source: Indeed, stimulation of PASMC with PTX3 preserved the expression of contractile markers in donor cells, but not in IPAH, while HGF downregulated contractile state markers in donor–IPAH and increased disease-state marker VCAN in IPAH-PASMC (Figure 7H).
claims.evidence: This is based on gene expression measurements after ligand stimulation shown in Figure 7H.

claims.claim: HGF downregulated contractile state markers in donor-IPAH and increased disease-state marker VCAN in IPAH-PASMC.
claims.source: Indeed, stimulation of PASMC with PTX3 preserved the expression of contractile markers in donor cells, but not in IPAH, while HGF downregulated contractile state markers in donor–IPAH and increased disease-state marker VCAN in IPAH-PASMC (Figure 7H).
claims.evidence: This is based on gene expression measurements after ligand stimulation shown in Figure 7H.

claims.claim: Upregulation of HGF/cMet pathway in endothelial cells upon Sox17 loss was associated with PAH promotion.

claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a study on HGF/cMet pathway in PAH.

claims.claim: SCARA5 is a ferritin scavenger receptor that mediates cellular iron uptake and limits the extracellular iron concentration.
claims.source: SCARA5, a ferritin scavenger receptor that mediates cellular iron uptake, limits the extracellular iron concentration (Li et al., 2009).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a study on SCARA5 function.

claims.claim: CFD activates the alternative pathway of the complement triggering chemotaxis and inflammation.
claims.source: CFD activates the alternative pathway of the complement triggering chemotaxis and inflammation (White et al., 1992).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a study on CFD function.

claims.claim: ADH1C is an enzyme involved in metabolism of lipid peroxidation products and hydroxysteroids.
claims.source: PAAF express ADH1C, enzyme involved in metabolism of lipid peroxidation products and hydroxysteroids (Höög and Ostberg, 2011), PPARG, a key transcriptional regulator of lipid metabolism, and APOE, a lipid handling protein (Source data 1 and Source data 2).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a study on ADH1C function.

claims.claim: RGS5 is a gatekeeper of G protein signaling and signal transduction modulator that influences and fine-tunes the PASMC response to external cue.
claims.source: RGS5, for instance, as a gatekeeper of G protein signaling and signal transduction modulator, influences and fine-tunes the PASMC response to external cue (Wang et al., 2008).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a study on RGS5 function.

claims.claim: Hexosamine biosynthetic pathway is a side branch of glycolysis utilized for generation of amino-sugars and subsequent protein and lipid glycosylation, including glycosaminoglycans and PG synthesis.
claims.source: Hexosamine biosynthetic pathway is a side branch of glycolysis utilized for generation of amino-sugars and subsequent protein and lipid glycosylation, including glycosaminoglycans and PG synthesis (Buse, 2006)
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a study on hexosamine pathway and represents established biochemical knowledge.

claims.claim: Proteoglycans can withstand high pressure, modulate cellular phenotype and be a necessary part of the adaptation or maladaptation process.
claims.source: Due to the complex structure of PG, they can withstand high pressure, modulate cellular phenotype and thus be a necessary part of the adaptation or maladaptation process (Wight and Merrilees, 2004).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a study on proteoglycan function.

claims.claim: Mitochondrial membrane hyperpolarization is linked with increased ROS production.
claims.source: Mitochondrial membrane hyperpolarization is linked with increased ROS production.
claims.evidence: This represents established knowledge about mitochondrial function.

claims.claim: Mitochondrial dysfunction and elevated ROS production are associated with increased apoptosis.
claims.source: Mitochondrial dysfunction and elevated ROS production are associated with increased apoptosis, aligning with reduced SOD2, which plays a role in clearing mitochondrial ROS and mitigating oxidative stress to protect against cell death (Kokoszka et al., 2001; Figure 4D).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citation and represents established knowledge about mitochondrial dysfunction and apoptosis.

claims.claim: SOD2 plays a role in clearing mitochondrial ROS and mitigating oxidative stress to protect against cell death.
claims.source: Mitochondrial dysfunction and elevated ROS production are associated with increased apoptosis, aligning with reduced SOD2, which plays a role in clearing mitochondrial ROS and mitigating oxidative stress to protect against cell death (Kokoszka et al., 2001; Figure 4D).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a study on SOD2 function.

claims.claim: Proteoglycans serve as regulators of the complement system.
claims.source: Among other functions, proteoglycans serve as regulators of the complement system (Clark et al., 2013).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a study on proteoglycan function in complement regulation.

claims.claim: ITGA2 and ITGB1 subunits expressed in PASMC build a heterodimer complex functioning both as laminin and collagen receptor.
claims.source: ITGA2 and ITGB1 subunits expressed in PASMC build a heterodimer complex functioning both as laminin and collagen receptor (Languino et al., 1989; Figure 6B).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a study on integrin function.

claims.claim: ECM class switching engages different high-affinity integrin receptors, which activate alternative downstream signaling pathways.

claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a study on integrin signaling and represents established knowledge.

claims.claim: Restoring SOD2 expression is a viable therapeutic target for pulmonary vascular disease.
claims.source: Whether mitochondrial disturbance is one the initial cause of the disease or its consequence, as a common point it offers a potential action point to revert cell states from different lineages toward a normal, homeostatic condition, in line with reports on restoring SOD2 expression as a viable therapeutic target (Paulin et al., 2014; Plecitá Hlavatá et al., 2023).
claims.evidence: This claim is inferred from the discussion of mitochondrial dysfunction as a common feature and is supported by citations to therapeutic studies.

claims.claim: Laminins and collagens act as PAAF-secreted ligands, regulating PASMC behavior through their ECM-sensing integrin receptors.

results.result: PASMC and PAAF display distinct molecular profiles in healthy donor cells. PCA analysis shows clear separation between cell types at both transcriptomic and proteomic levels, with PASMC showing higher interpersonal heterogeneity. Cell-type-specific markers (RGS5, IGFBP5 for PASMC; ADH1C, SCARA5, CFD for PAAF) localize to appropriate tissue compartments. Functional enrichment analysis reveals PASMC enrichment in vascular development and ECM organization, while PAAF shows enrichment in mitochondrial metabolism and lipid homeostasis.
results.evaluation: Claims C22-C31 are well-supported by multiple lines of evidence including PCA analysis (Figure 1B), immunofluorescent staining and in situ hybridization (Figures 1D-E), and GSEA/overrepresentation analysis (Figures 1F-G). The data consistently demonstrate distinct molecular profiles between cell types with appropriate validation methods.

results.result: PASMC and PAAF exhibit distinct metabolic profiles. PASMC can equally utilize glucose/pyruvate and fatty acids for oxidative metabolism, while PAAF shows stronger dependence on fatty acid oxidation. PAAF displays lower OCR and ECAR, higher OCR/ECAR ratio indicating preference for oxidative phosphorylation, and lower glycolytic capacity and mitochondrial proton leak compared to PASMC.
results.evaluation: Claims C32-C37 are supported by Seahorse metabolic analyzer measurements (Figures 1H-I and Figure 1—figure supplement 2). The data show consistent metabolic differences between cell types with appropriate statistical comparisons (n=6). The findings align with the transcriptomic enrichment for mitochondrial processes in PAAF.

results.result: PASMC and PAAF retain their core cellular identities while acquiring distinct disease-associated states in IPAH. PCA shows cell type as a stronger discriminant than disease state. OPLS-DA modeling finds significant separation based on cell type but not disease state alone; only transcriptomic data shows significant separation when considering both factors simultaneously. Cell-type-specific markers remain localized to appropriate compartments in IPAH tissue.
results.evaluation: Claims C38-C41, C11-C12 are supported by PCA and OPLS-DA analyses (Figures 2A-C) and immunofluorescent validation (Figures 2D-E). The statistical modeling appropriately demonstrates that cell lineage identity is preserved despite disease-associated transcriptional changes. This is further corroborated by single-cell RNA-seq data and citations to fate-mapping studies.

results.result: IPAH-PASMC display a synthetic phenotype characterized by upregulation of biosynthetic processes (nucleotide-sugar, lipid biosynthesis, Golgi transport, ER stress) and downregulation of contractile machinery (cytoskeletal components, p53 signaling). This is accompanied by increased glycosaminoglycan production in IPAH pulmonary arteries, with enhanced medial and neointimal staining.
results.evaluation: Claims C42-C43, C5-C6, C46-C47 are supported by GO analysis (Figure 3A), biochemical GAG quantification (Figure 3B, n=7-8), and histological staining with quantitative image analysis (Figures 3C-D, n=10). The multiple complementary approaches provide strong evidence for the synthetic phenotype of IPAH-PASMC.

results.result: IPAH-PAAF display a hyperproliferative phenotype with upregulation of cell cycle and DNA repair processes, and downregulation of NF-κB pathway components. IPAH-PAAF show higher proliferative capacity than donor-PAAF in both stimulated and unstimulated conditions, while IPAH-PASMC show lower proliferation than donor-PASMC. This phenotypic effect is strongest in early passage and progressively lost with passaging. In situ, PCNA+ fibroblasts are frequently observed in IPAH adventitia.
results.evaluation: Claims C44-C45, C7, C48-C51 are supported by GO analysis (Figure 3A), [3H]thymidine incorporation assays (Figure 3E, n=5-6), cell counting across passages (Figure 3F), and immunofluorescent staining (Figure 3G). The convergence of in vitro and in situ data strengthens the conclusion about the hyperproliferative IPAH-PAAF phenotype.

results.result: Early-passage cultured cells partially retain disease-specific phenotypic features observed in fresh cells. IPAH-PASMC retain enrichment for biosynthetic and ECM processes in early passage, while both early and late-passage IPAH-PAAF display enrichment for cell cycle processes. However, there are prominent inverse enrichments for inflammatory/NF-κB signaling between fresh and cultured IPAH-PAAF.
results.evaluation: Claims C52-C54, C17 are supported by GSEA comparing fresh, early-passage, and late-passage cells (Figure 3H) using published datasets. The analysis appropriately identifies both preserved and lost features with culture, though the inverse enrichment for inflammatory processes in PAAF represents a significant limitation of the culture system.

results.result: IPAH-PASMC and IPAH-PAAF share limited common molecular perturbations (47 co-directionally regulated genes/proteins) that converge on immuno-inflammatory and survival-apoptosis pathways. Both cell types share mitochondrial dysfunction characterized by reduced mitochondrial content under starvation and hyperpolarized mitochondrial membrane potential.
results.evaluation: Claims C55-C57, C3-C4, C58-C59 are supported by differential expression analysis (Figure 4A), STRING network analysis (Figure 4C), BioPlanet pathway enrichment (Figure 4D), and TMRM staining measurements (Figures 4E-F). The convergence on mitochondrial dysfunction as a shared feature is well-documented, though the functional consequences appear cell-type specific.

results.result: Only IPAH-PASMC significantly upregulate ROS production upon PDGF-BB stimulation, despite both cell types showing mitochondrial dysfunction.
results.evaluation: Claim C60 is supported by CellRox measurements (Figure 4G) with appropriate sample sizes and statistical testing. This demonstrates cell-type-specific downstream consequences of shared mitochondrial dysfunction.

results.result: PASMC and PAAF acquire divergent disease-cell states in IPAH. PASMC show more pronounced changes with downregulated molecules primarily from PASMC-enriched healthy state genes, while upregulated molecules come from both cell types. IPAH-regulated molecules in PAAF trace back to both cell types. GO analysis reveals PASMC harbor ECM-related changes while PAAF show cell cycle/replication enrichment.
results.evaluation: Claims C61-C66 are supported by differential expression analysis (Figure 5B), STRING network analysis with cell-type origin overlay (Figure 5B), and GO analysis (Figure 5C). The data demonstrate clear cell-type-specific disease trajectories with appropriate bioinformatic approaches.

results.result: ECM composition (laminin vs. collagen) elicits cell-type and cell-state specific phenotypic responses. Cells on collagen show spread-out morphology while laminin inhibits spreading. PASMC (both donor and IPAH) attach less efficiently to laminin than collagen, while only donor-PAAF show this preference. PAAF show faster gap closure than PASMC on both substrates. These findings support laminin and collagen as PAAF-derived regulators of PASMC phenotype.
results.evaluation: Claims C67-C73, C8 are supported by microscopy observations (Figure 6C), attachment assays (Figure 6D, n=5-6), and gap closure assays (Figure 6E, n=2-6). The data demonstrate functional consequences of ECM composition changes, though some comparisons lack statistical significance (C71) and sample sizes vary.

results.result: Integrin receptor expression profiles differ between PASMC and PAAF. High-affinity collagen and laminin receptor subunits show higher expression in cultured PASMC compared to PAAF with minimal disease-state changes. In fresh cells, IPAH-PAAF display increased expression of alpha2 and alpha6 integrin subunits.
results.evaluation: Claims C74-C75 are supported by gene expression data from cultured cells (Figure 6F) and single-cell transcriptomics from fresh cells (Figure 6G). The data provide molecular basis for differential ECM responses, though the discrepancy between cultured and fresh cell patterns warrants consideration.

results.result: Complement activation induces cell-type-specific proteoglycan expression. Both VCAN and DCN show higher expression in IPAH cells. Only donor-PAAF respond to C3a and C5a stimulation with IPAH-state-like DCN expression levels.
results.evaluation: Claims C76-C77 are supported by gene expression measurements after complement stimulation (Figures 6H-I, n=4-6). The data demonstrate an autocrine feedback loop in PAAF linking complement activation to ECM production, though statistical significance is not clearly indicated for all comparisons.

results.result: IPAH-PAAF modulate PASMC phenotype through secreted factors. CellChat analysis reveals skewed PAAF-to-PASMC signaling toward secreted ligands in IPAH. Co-culture of donor-PASMC with IPAH-PAAF leads to partial loss of healthy state markers (CNN1, RHOA) without affecting disease-state markers, while donor-PAAF markers are unaffected by IPAH-PASMC co-culture. Bulk RNA-Seq shows upregulated genes in PASMC mediate inflammatory processes, apoptosis, and proliferation.
results.evaluation: Claims C78-C82 are supported by CellChat analysis (Figure 7A), combined CellChat/NicheNet analysis (Figure 7B), qRT-PCR from co-cultures (Figure 7D, n=3), and bulk RNA-Seq with GSEA (Figure 7E). The directional nature of PAAF-to-PASMC signaling is well-demonstrated, though the mild effect size required model correction for paired samples.

results.result: PTX3 and HGF are PAAF-derived regulators of PASMC phenotype with opposing effects. PTX3 (downregulated in IPAH-PAAF) preserves contractile marker expression in donor-PASMC but not IPAH-PASMC. HGF (upregulated in IPAH-PAAF) downregulates contractile markers in donor-PASMC and increases disease-state marker VCAN in IPAH-PASMC.
results.evaluation: Claims C9-C10, C83-C84 are supported by secretome analysis (Figures 7F-G) and gene expression measurements after ligand stimulation (Figure 7H, n=6). The identification of PTX3 and HGF as opposing regulators is well-supported, though the differential response of donor vs. IPAH-PASMC to PTX3 requires further investigation.

results.result: Pulmonary vascular remodeling is characterized by functional alterations in PASMC and PAAF, with distinct phenotypic shifts during disease progression.
results.evaluation: Claims C1-C2 represent the overarching findings of the study, supported by the comprehensive transcriptomic, proteomic, and phenotypic characterization presented throughout. These summary claims are well-supported by the totality of evidence.

results.result: Prior studies establish that vascular cells retain lineage identity during remodeling while acquiring altered expression profiles and functional changes. Previous work by the authors showed skewed cellular communication in pulmonary vascular disease, and cultured cells from remodeled arteries display metabolic and inflammatory reprogramming.
results.evaluation: Claims C13-C16, C18-C20 are supported by appropriate citations to published literature. These claims establish the scientific context and prior knowledge foundation for the current study.

results.result: The study used early-passage PASMC and PAAF isolated from the same pulmonary artery of healthy donors or IPAH patients.
results.evaluation: Claim C21 describes the experimental design, which is clearly documented in the methods section and Figure 1A. This represents appropriate experimental design for source-matched comparisons.

results.result: Background knowledge claims about molecular functions: SCARA5 mediates iron uptake, CFD activates complement, ADH1C metabolizes lipid peroxidation products, RGS5 modulates G protein signaling, hexosamine pathway generates amino-sugars, proteoglycans withstand pressure and regulate complement, mitochondrial hyperpolarization links to ROS production, SOD2 clears mitochondrial ROS, integrins function as ECM receptors with specific signaling pathways.
results.evaluation: Claims C87-C98 represent established biological knowledge supported by appropriate citations. These provide necessary context for interpreting the experimental findings.

results.result: Upregulation of HGF/cMet pathway in endothelial cells upon Sox17 loss was associated with PAH promotion in a prior study.
results.evaluation: Claim C86 is supported by citation to Park et al., 2022. This provides relevant context for the HGF findings in the current study.

results.result: Restoring SOD2 expression is proposed as a viable therapeutic target for pulmonary vascular disease based on the common mitochondrial dysfunction observed.
results.evaluation: Claim C99 is inferred from the mitochondrial dysfunction findings and supported by citations to therapeutic studies. However, the current study does not directly test SOD2 restoration, and the lack of detectable apoptosis in situ (Figure 4H) raises questions about the functional significance of the observed mitochondrial changes.

results.result: A proposed model suggests laminins and collagens act as PAAF-secreted ligands regulating PASMC behavior through integrin receptors, with PASMC susceptibility traced to enriched integrin expression.
results.evaluation: Claims C100-C101 represent a mechanistic model inferred from the ECM response data, integrin expression patterns, and functional assays. The model is reasonable given the supporting data, though direct mechanistic validation would strengthen the conclusion.

results.result: The removal of PAAF from their native immunomodulatory environment and hydrocortisone in culture media could explain inverse enrichment of inflammatory processes in cultured versus fresh PAAF.
results.evaluation: Claim C102 is speculation about the cause of observed culture-induced changes. While plausible, this hypothesis is not directly tested and represents a limitation acknowledgment rather than a supported finding.

results.result: A potential exploratory clinical trial could combine recombinant PTX3 and HGF blocking antibody or c-Met inhibitor for pulmonary vascular disease treatment.
results.evaluation: Claim C103 is a speculative therapeutic proposal based on the PTX3 and HGF findings. While the rationale is supported by the data, this represents a future direction rather than a tested conclusion. The proposal lacks consideration of potential off-target effects and the complexity of in vivo systems.

results.result: The identified PAAF-derived factors likely represent a fraction of ligands in the pulmonary artery compartment, and the influence of endothelial and inflammatory cells requires further investigation.
results.evaluation: Claims C104-C105 appropriately acknowledge study limitations and identify gaps for future research. These represent reasonable caveats given the focused scope on PASMC-PAAF interactions.

results.result: Low case number and end-stage disease samples represent study limitations that must be considered before generalizing findings to the entire PAH patient population.
results.evaluation: Claim C106 is an explicit and appropriate acknowledgment of study limitations. The sample size (n=4 per group for omics) is indeed limited, and the use of end-stage disease samples may not reflect earlier disease stages.

results.result: The study characterized source-matched early-passage PASMC and PAAF from healthy donors and IPAH patients using transcriptomic and proteomic profiling. PCA analysis showed clear separation by cell type with PASMC displaying higher interpersonal heterogeneity. Cell-type-specific markers were validated in tissue, and functional characterization revealed distinct metabolic profiles between the two cell types.
results.evaluation: Reviewers explicitly praised this as 'one of the first studies using orthogonal sequencing and phenotyping for characterization of source-matched neighboring mesenchymal PASMC and PAAF cells' and noted 'technical rigor is quite high in the -omics methodology.' The editor confirmed the study 'identified distinct disease-related states in each cell type' with 'convincing and robust' findings.

results.result: PASMC and PAAF retain their core cellular identities during disease while acquiring distinct disease-associated states. OPLS-DA modeling showed cell type as a stronger discriminant than disease state, though transcriptomic data revealed significant separation when considering both factors simultaneously.
results.evaluation: Reviewers acknowledged this finding, with one noting 'the authors revealed that PASMC and PAAF retained their original cellular identity and acquired different states associated with the pathogenesis of PAH.' The editor confirmed the study 'identified distinct disease-related states in each cell type.' No concerns were raised about this core conclusion.

results.result: IPAH-PASMC exhibit increased glycosaminoglycan production, downregulation of contractile machinery, and upregulation of biosynthetic processes. This was demonstrated through transcriptomic/proteomic analysis, biochemical assays, and histological staining showing enhanced GAG content in IPAH pulmonary arteries.
results.evaluation: Reviewers highlighted this as an 'interesting and surprising finding' and noted the 'inherent comparative organization of the study' aided understanding of 'distinct IPAH-associated cell states.' The editor confirmed findings were 'convincing and robust' supported by 'advanced and complementary techniques.' No methodological concerns were raised about these specific measurements.

results.result: IPAH-PAAF display a hyperproliferative phenotype with upregulated cell cycle and DNA repair processes, while IPAH-PASMC show lower proliferative rates. This differential proliferation was strongest in early passage and progressively lost with passaging, and was validated in tissue sections.
results.evaluation: Reviewers specifically noted 'interesting and surprising findings in the cellular characterizations, including the low proliferative state of IPAH-PASMCs as compared to the hyperproliferative state in IPAH-PAAFs.' The editor confirmed findings were 'convincing and robust.' The passage-dependent nature of the phenotype was acknowledged without criticism.

results.result: IPAH-PASMC and IPAH-PAAF share limited common features including reduced mitochondrial content and hyperpolarization. Only 47 genes/proteins were co-directionally regulated, converging on immuno-inflammatory and apoptosis pathways. IPAH-PASMC specifically showed increased ROS production upon stimulation.
results.evaluation: Reviewers noted the study revealed 'distinct phenotypic shifts during pulmonary vascular remodeling, with limited shared features.' The editor confirmed the study 'provided deeper insights into their interactions and communication.' No concerns were raised about the mitochondrial measurements or the limited overlap between cell types.

results.result: Alterations in extracellular matrix components (laminin and collagen) regulate PASMC phenotypic responses. PASMC showed differential attachment and migration on collagen versus laminin substrates, with IPAH-PASMC displaying altered responses. PASMC expressed higher levels of integrin receptors for these ECM components compared to PAAF.
results.evaluation: Reviewers highlighted 'cell-cell communication axes involving ECM components and soluble ligands provided by PAAFs that direct cell state dynamics of PASMCs' as providing 'some of the first and foundational descriptions.' The editor confirmed findings on 'interactions and communication' were convincing. No methodological concerns were raised about the adhesion or migration assays.

results.result: Pentraxin-3 and hepatocyte growth factor are potential regulators of PASMC phenotypic transitions mediated by PAAF. CellChat analysis revealed skewed PAAF-to-PASMC signaling in IPAH. Co-culture and stimulation experiments showed PTX3 preserves contractile markers in donor PASMC while HGF downregulates them and increases disease markers.
results.evaluation: Reviewers specifically praised findings on 'cell-cell communication axes involving ECM components and soluble ligands provided by PAAFs that direct cell state dynamics of PASMCs' as 'some of the first and foundational descriptions.' The editor confirmed the study 'provided deeper insights into their interactions and communication.' The functional validation experiments were not criticized.

results.result: Molecular alterations identified in fresh cells are at least partially preserved in early-passage cultured cells. Early-passage IPAH-PASMC retain biosynthetic and ECM enrichments, while IPAH-PAAF show prominent cell cycle enrichment across passages. However, there are inverse enrichments for inflammatory/NF-κB signaling between fresh and cultured PAAF.
results.evaluation: While reviewers acknowledged the authors 'addressed this concern appropriately with significant text changes to clarify these limitations,' they maintained that 'the major limitation of the impact and conclusions of the paper is that the full extent of the relevance of these findings to human disease is not known' due to use of cultured cells. The inverse inflammatory enrichment in cultured versus fresh PAAF highlights this limitation.

results.result: PASMC showed more pronounced molecular changes than PAAF in IPAH, with downregulated molecules primarily from PASMC-enriched genes in healthy state and upregulated molecules from both cell types. GO analysis revealed PASMC harbored ECM-related changes while PAAF showed cell cycle enrichment.
results.evaluation: Reviewers noted 'the inherent comparative organization of the study and presentation of the data were valuable in aiding the reader in understanding how to discern the distinct IPAH-associated cell states.' The editor confirmed findings were 'convincing and robust.' No concerns were raised about these comparative molecular analyses.

results.result: VCAN and DCN showed higher expression in IPAH cells, with donor-PAAF responding to complement stimulation (C3a and C5a) by displaying IPAH-like DCN expression levels.
results.evaluation: These findings were part of the ECM and cell-cell communication results that reviewers praised as providing 'foundational descriptions.' No specific concerns were raised about the complement stimulation experiments or gene expression measurements.

results.result: The study acknowledges limitations including low case numbers and use of end-stage disease samples, which may limit generalizability to all IPAH patients or across disease progression stages.
results.evaluation: Reviewers explicitly noted 'the number of donors sampled for PAAF/PASMCs was relatively small' and that this 'should temper the conclusions,' though they acknowledged 'the authors addressed this concern with important text changes and additional data.' The editor noted 'certain conclusions should be interpreted with caution due to inherent methodological limitations.'

comparisons.comparison: Both evaluate the foundational characterization of PASMC and PAAF cells (C22-C31 overlap). OpenEval focuses on molecular profiling evidence (PCA, immunofluorescence, GSEA), while peer reviewers praised the technical rigor and orthogonal sequencing methodology. Both find the characterization well-supported. Peer review also includes metabolic findings (C32-C37) and experimental design (C21) not separated by OpenEval.

OpenEval R2 addresses metabolic differences (C32-C37) with Seahorse data, which peer reviewers included in their broader assessment of the foundational characterization. Both find evidence convincing, though peer review does not separately evaluate metabolic claims.

Perfect claim overlap (C38-C41, C11-C12). Both agree that lineage identity preservation despite disease changes is well-supported. OpenEval emphasizes PCA/OPLS-DA statistical modeling and immunofluorescent validation, while peer reviewers highlight this as a core conclusion about distinct disease-related states in each cell type.

Perfect claim overlap (C42-C43, C5-C6, C46-C47). Both strongly support the synthetic phenotype of IPAH-PASMC. OpenEval details multiple complementary approaches (GO analysis, GAG quantification, histological staining), while peer reviewers called this an 'interesting and surprising finding' with convincing evidence.

Perfect claim overlap (C44-C45, C7, C48-C51). Both support the hyperproliferative IPAH-PAAF phenotype. OpenEval emphasizes convergence of in vitro and in situ data, while peer reviewers specifically highlighted the surprising contrast between low proliferative IPAH-PASMC and hyperproliferative IPAH-PAAF as convincing and robust.

Perfect claim overlap (C52-C54, C17). OpenEval finds culture system limitations appropriately identified through GSEA, marking preserved and lost features. Peer reviewers express more concern, rating this UNCERTAIN due to relevance to human disease, noting the inverse inflammatory enrichment as a significant limitation despite authors' clarifications.

High overlap on mitochondrial dysfunction claims (C55-C59, C3-C4). OpenEval includes C58-C59 not in peer review, while peer review includes C60. Both support shared mitochondrial dysfunction with cell-type-specific consequences. OpenEval details convergent evidence from multiple analyses, peer reviewers note distinct phenotypic shifts with limited shared features.

OpenEval R8 addresses ROS specifically (C60), which peer reviewers included in their broader mitochondrial dysfunction assessment (R5). Both find the cell-type-specific downstream consequences well-supported by CellRox measurements.

Perfect claim overlap (C61-C66). Both strongly support cell-type-specific disease trajectories. OpenEval emphasizes bioinformatic approaches (differential expression, STRING, GO analysis), while peer reviewers praised the comparative organization aiding understanding of distinct IPAH-associated cell states.

High overlap on ECM functional consequences (C67-C73, C8). OpenEval notes some comparisons lack statistical significance and varying sample sizes but finds claims supported. Peer reviewers praised ECM and cell-cell communication findings as 'foundational descriptions' without raising methodological concerns about adhesion/migration assays.

OpenEval R11 addresses molecular basis for differential ECM responses (C74-C75), which peer reviewers included in their broader ECM/communication assessment. Both support the findings, though OpenEval notes discrepancy between cultured and fresh cell patterns warrants consideration.

Perfect claim overlap (C76-C77). Both support the autocrine feedback loop in PAAF linking complement activation to ECM production. OpenEval notes statistical significance not clearly indicated for all comparisons, while peer reviewers included this in praised 'foundational descriptions' without specific concerns.

High overlap on PAAF-to-PASMC signaling (C78-C82). OpenEval finds directional signaling well-demonstrated despite mild effect size. Peer reviewers specifically praised cell-cell communication findings involving ECM and soluble ligands as 'first and foundational descriptions.' Both strongly support these claims.

Partial overlap on PTX3 and HGF as opposing regulators (C9-C10, C83-C84). OpenEval finds identification well-supported but notes differential PTX3 response requires investigation. Peer reviewers included these in praised cell-cell communication findings without raising specific concerns about the ligand stimulation experiments.

Partial overlap (C1-C2 vs C2, C106). OpenEval finds overarching summary claims (C1-C2) well-supported by totality of evidence. Peer reviewers acknowledge the findings (C2) but emphasize sample size limitations (C106) should temper conclusions, noting inherent methodological limitations require cautious interpretation.

OpenEval R16 evaluates literature-based contextual claims (C13-C16, C18-C20) as appropriately supported by citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background/context claims.

OpenEval R17 evaluates experimental design (C21) as clearly documented and appropriate. Peer reviewers included C21 in their broader foundational characterization assessment (R1), praising the source-matched comparative approach without separate evaluation.
OpenEval R18 evaluates established biological knowledge claims (C87-C98) as appropriately supported by citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these contextual claims.
OpenEval R19 evaluates HGF context claim (C86) as supported by citation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific contextual claim.

OpenEval rates SOD2 restoration claim (C99) as UNCERTAIN, noting lack of direct testing and questions about functional significance given no detectable apoptosis. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this therapeutic inference.

OpenEval finds mechanistic model about ECM-integrin interactions (C100-C101) supported but notes direct validation would strengthen conclusions. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific mechanistic model.

OpenEval rates speculation about culture-induced changes (C102) as UNCERTAIN, noting it represents limitation acknowledgment rather than tested finding. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, though peer R8 addresses broader culture limitations.

OpenEval rates therapeutic proposal (C103) as UNCERTAIN, noting it represents future direction rather than tested conclusion and lacks consideration of complexity. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this speculative therapeutic claim.

OpenEval finds limitation acknowledgments (C104-C105) appropriately stated regarding gaps in understanding other cell types. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific limitation statements.

Both address study limitations (C106). OpenEval finds the acknowledgment of small sample size and end-stage disease samples appropriate. Peer reviewers explicitly noted the small donor number should temper conclusions, acknowledging authors addressed concerns with text changes but maintaining cautious interpretation is warranted.
